name: Shadowfang Keep
summary: In southern Silverpine, Shadowfang Keep shelters the rogue Kirin Tor wizard Archmage Arugal and the worgen he summoned. The old Silverlaine estate now holds feral beasts and the phantoms of its slaughtered defenders, while nearby Pyrewood Village remains bound to a horrifying curse.

sections.title: Fall of the Silverlaine Dynasty
sections.body: Shadowfang Keep was once Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat defended by the pious Commander Springvale. During the Third War, the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied the Kirin Tor leadership and turned to the research of the wizard Ur. He summoned extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The beasts savaged the undead, then slipped beyond mortal control and stormed southern Silverpine. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls beside the feral monsters that overran their home.

sections.title: Arugal's Children
sections.body: Broken by guilt and madness, Arugal withdrew behind the blood-stained battlements. He called the ravenous wolf-men his beloved children and named the castle Shadowfang Keep. In its stone roosts, lupine packs and shadowy hounds thrive under trainers such as Wolf Master Nandos, watched by Arugal's massive lupine beast, Fenrus the Devourer. The curse did not halt at the walls. Nearby Pyrewood Village remains trapped in a horrifying nocturnal cycle: its people walk as men by day and hunt as ravenous worgen beneath the moon, bound to the mad archmage on the heights above.

sections.title: The Forsaken Strike
sections.body: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner saw Arugal as a dire threat to her dominion in Silverpine Forest and sent the Royal Apothecary Society and elite Deathstalkers to find the source of the worgen curse. Infiltration teams suffered brutal losses in the dungeons, but Horde heroes answering the call from the Sepulcher eventually break into the highest tower. When they strike down Arugal, the pack loses its master. The mind directing the beasts' spread through the wilderness is severed, and his head becomes proof of Lordaeron's vengeance.

faq.q: What happens when Archmage Arugal is defeated?
faq.answer: Slaying Arugal removes the central force controlling the worgen packs in southern Silverpine. On Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Horde adventurers take his severed head to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. The feral beasts and ghostly remnants in the keep and surrounding woods remain a danger to travelers.

faq.q: Why did Arugal summon the worgen?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Dalaran's armies suffered disastrous defeats against the Scourge, and fallen wizards kept rising as undead soldiers for the Lich King. Seeking a weapon to turn the tide, Arugal used the research of the wizard Ur to summon extra-dimensional worgen, believing their savagery could halt the Scourge.

Baron Silverlaine was the human nobleman who ruled the keep and oversaw nearby Pyrewood before the Third War. When Arugal's summoned beasts escaped control, they stormed the stronghold and killed the baron, his household, and his guards. Silverlaine's vengeful ghost still haunts the great dining halls, cursed to walk beside the monsters that slew him.

faq.q: Why are Pyrewood Village villagers friendly during the day?
faq.answer: Arugal's dark magic left the people of nearby Pyrewood Village human, clear-minded, and peaceful toward Alliance travelers by day. At sundown, the curse takes hold and transforms the entire population into savage worgen loyal to the mad archmage in the keep.

Commander Springvale was a paladin and the military officer responsible for defending Silverlaine Keep. When the worgen overran the stronghold, he fought to the death. His restless spirit still patrols the upper hallways, clinging to martial duty even in undeath.

faq.q: What is the Book of Ur?
faq.answer: The Book of Ur holds the research of Ur, an archmage of Dalaran who studied extra-dimensional entities, including the worgen. Arugal used the writings to make his disastrous summons. The Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity seeks the book to understand the wolf-creatures and their strange magic.

angles.text: The Forsaken see Arugal's encroaching packs as an immediate danger to their fledgling territory in Silverpine. Deathstalker operatives and the Royal Apothecary Society make the keep a priority target.
As a mage, Shadowfang's tragedy warns what can happen when a Kirin Tor wizard meddles with extra-dimensional summoning beyond mortal control.
As a warlock, you may be drawn to the keep's dark energies, voidwalkers, and fell sorceries, and to the search for ancient relics such as the Orb of Soran'ruk.
As a paladin, you may see Commander Springvale's restless spirit as a sorrowful reminder of fallen paladin defenders whose sacred oaths were warped by death.
